Short answer: Month-to-date P&L (2026‑10‑01→2026‑10‑13) shows a net profit of −₹219,593, an improvement vs the prior period (2026‑09‑17→2026‑09‑29) which had −₹1,185,278; the change is driven mainly by a large rise in P&L ad spend (worsening profit) offset by an even larger improvement in contribution margin (helping profit). 

What the data shows
- Totals (event window vs prior): P&L net profit −₹219,593 ← −₹1,185,278; P&L ad spend ₹708,880 ← ₹293,571; P&L contribution margin ₹489,287 ← −₹891,706.  
- Bridge (accounting identity): higher ad spend reduced profit by ~₹451,364 (47% of the P&L change) while contribution margin increased profit by ~₹1,407,840 (147% of the change); the arithmetic reconciles exactly.  
- Where it moved: platform-level shifts matter — Meta and Google both moved substantially (Meta’s segment moved ~38% of the change); a few ads/adsets had outsized swings (examples flagged in the diagnosis).  
- Data caveats: 2026‑10‑14 is partial and excluded; a few tax lines failed to fetch but do not break the reconciliation.

Worth checking: drill P&L ad spend and contribution margin by channel → campaign → ad to see which campaigns raised spend without profitable returns.
